newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan banks plan merger to become top 10 firm.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan banks plan merger to become top 10 firm.

text.p: Kazakhstan banks Caspiyskiy and Kazdorbank plan to merge to become one of the top 10 in the local industry and focus on oil and construction projects, bank officials said on Wednesday.
"We want to become a more stable structure and enter the ranks of the first 10 Kazakh banks," Nina Gorina, board chairman at Kazdorbank, told Reuters.
Both banks will hold shareholder meetings on August 15 to take final decisions on the plan.
"Shareholders of both banks will win much more than they will lose in this merger," said Askar Yelemesov, vice chairman of Caspiyskiy. "This is a winning situation."
Yelemesov said the united bank would focus on Kazakhstan oil projects, chiefly involving Russia's largest oil producer LUKoil, which has a 25 percent stake in Caspiyskiy.

Such projects include developing the large Kumkol oil field in the Central Asian state's south, exploring oil reserves on the Caspian Sea shelf and building an oil pipeline from the giant Tengiz oil field to the Black Sea.
Kazakhstan is developing huge energy reserves.
"The united bank will also take part in construction projects in Kazakhstan's new capital, Akmola," Yelemesov said.

Kazdorbank, organised from the structures of the former Soviet republic's ministry of automobile roads in 1989, has capital of 150 million tenge ($2 million) and chiefly services companies involved in building houses, roads and bridges.
Caspiyskiy pretax profit for the first half of 1997 was 17.24 million tenge. Caspiyskiy was founded in 1991 and has capital of 120 million tenge.
Kazdorbank's first half pretax profit was a mere 31,000 tenge, due to massive provisions made for possible losses from overdue loans.
Kazakhstan's banking system currently has 96 banks, including six state-run ones, one interstate and nine banks with foreign capital.
